```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5, dpi = 150)
has_cebmf <- requireNamespace("basilisk", quietly = TRUE) ||
  !is.null(getOption("cellprograms.cebmf_python_env"))
```

`fit_celltype_programs()` ships two interchangeable EBMF backends:

| | `backend = "flashier"` (default) | `backend = "cebmf_torch"` |
|---|---|---|
| Implementation | R (flashier.utils) | Python (torch, covariate-EBMF) |
| Failure mode | nullcheck fallback ladder | fails loudly, no fallback |
| ELBO | reported | `NA` (not produced; the trace is) |
| Convergence record | ELBO trace | `objective_trace` |

Everything around the factorization — preprocessing, canonicalization,
program extraction, plots, sharing — is backend-agnostic. This vignette runs
the torch backend on a small simulated count dataset and shows where the two
contracts differ.

## Python environment

The torch backend needs a Python environment with `torch`, `numpy`, `scipy`,
`pandas`, and `cebmf_torch`. By default the package uses a **basilisk-managed
environment** with pinned versions (Python 3.11, `torch==2.7.1` CPU build,
`cebmf_torch` at a pinned commit), built automatically on first use and
cached across sessions. To point at your own environment instead:

```{r env-option, eval = FALSE}
options(cellprograms.cebmf_python_env = "/path/to/venv")  # venv dir or python binary
```

## Input regime: normalize counts first

The torch backend estimates column-wise noise and **diverges immediately on
raw unnormalized Gaussian-scale matrices** (the objective goes non-finite at
iteration 0; the backend fails loudly rather than returning a garbage fit —
this is by design and is the documented reason the test suite's registered
fixture normalizes counts). Feed it what the single-cell pipeline produces:
counts, size-factor normalization, log1p, gene z-scaling.

```{r recipe}
library(cellprograms)
set.seed(3)
n <- 60; g <- 400; p <- 2

# block-structured counts: 2 planted programs over private gene sets
W <- matrix(0, g, p)
for (j in seq_len(p)) W[sample.int(g, 60), j] <- runif(60, 0.5, 1.5)
S <- matrix(0, n, p)
for (j in seq_len(p)) S[sample.int(n, 20), j] <- runif(20, 1, 2.5)
lam <- exp(pmin(pmax(S %*% t(W), 0), 4)) + 0.05
counts <- matrix(rpois(n * g, as.vector(lam)), n, g)

# size-factor log1p + gene z-scale: the backend's input regime
sf <- rowSums(counts); sf <- sf / mean(sf)
Y <- scale(log1p(counts / sf))
dimnames(Y) <- list(paste0("s", seq_len(n)), paste0("g", seq_len(g)))

x <- as_cell_program_data(list(CT1 = Y))
validate_cell_program_data(x)
```

## Fit with the torch backend

```{r fit, eval = has_cebmf}
fit <- fit_celltype_programs(x, backend = "cebmf_torch",
                             max_factors = 6, seed = 1)
fl <- fit$fits$CT1$flash
fl$backend
fl$n_factors
head(fl$objective_trace)   # convergence record (the torch backend's ELBO analogue)
```

The registered mapping contract: the torch backend does not produce an ELBO,
so `program_summary()` reports `NA` there and nothing is manufactured to fill
the gap; `objective_trace` is the honest convergence record. Loadings and
scores arrive in the same shapes as the flashier backend:

```{r shapes, eval = has_cebmf}
dim(fl$L_pm)   # samples x factors
dim(fl$F_pm)   # genes x factors
```

## Determinism at a fixed seed

```{r determinism, eval = has_cebmf}
fit2 <- fit_celltype_programs(x, backend = "cebmf_torch",
                              max_factors = 6, seed = 1)
identical(fit$fits$CT1$flash$L_pm, fit2$fits$CT1$flash$L_pm)
```

## var_floor passes through

`var_floor` (a positive scalar) is forwarded to the torch fit as a known
noise standard deviation, replacing the column-wise noise estimate:

```{r varfloor, eval = has_cebmf}
fit3 <- fit_celltype_programs(x, backend = "cebmf_torch",
                              max_factors = 6, seed = 1, var_floor = 0.5)
all(is.finite(fit3$fits$CT1$flash$objective_trace))
```

## Covariate adjustment (residualize mode)

Sample-level covariates are regressed out of the pseudobulk before
factorization — pass column names of `sample_metadata` (or a one-sided
formula). To show the adjustment doing real work, plant a known batch effect
(a global shift on a nuisance gene set for the `b2` samples), fit with and
without adjustment, and compare how much program activity aligns with batch:

```{r covariates, eval = has_cebmf}
batch_genes <- sort(sample.int(g, 60))
batch <- rep(c("b1", "b2"), c(40, 20))
Yb <- Y
Yb[batch == "b2", batch_genes] <- Yb[batch == "b2", batch_genes] + 1.2
meta <- data.frame(observation_id = rownames(Yb), batch = batch)
x_batch <- as_cell_program_data(list(CT1 = Yb), sample_metadata = meta)

fit_raw <- fit_celltype_programs(x_batch, backend = "cebmf_torch",
                                 max_factors = 6, seed = 1)
fit_adj <- fit_celltype_programs(x_batch, backend = "cebmf_torch",
                                 covariates = "batch",
                                 max_factors = 6, seed = 1)

batch_num <- as.numeric(batch == "b2")
max_batch_corr <- function(fit) {
  Z <- fit$scores$CT1
  if (is.null(Z) || ncol(Z) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  max(abs(apply(Z, 2, cor, y = batch_num)))
}
round(c(unadjusted = max_batch_corr(fit_raw),
        adjusted   = max_batch_corr(fit_adj)), 3)
```

The unadjusted fit devotes its strongest component to the batch shift; after
`covariates = "batch"` the alignment drops and the planted programs — which
are independent of batch — carry the factorization instead.

Two contract notes: `covariate_mode = "fixed"` (covariates as fixed loadings
inside the factorization) is **flashier-only** — the torch backend aborts
with guidance rather than silently residualizing. And the covariate design
must leave at least 10 residual degrees of freedom in every cell type; the
fit fails closed otherwise.

## Downstream is backend-agnostic

```{r downstream, eval = has_cebmf}
fit <- canonicalize_programs(fit)
program_summary(fit)[, c("cell_type", "n_obs", "n_programs", "R2", "elbo")]

pid <- head(colnames(program_scores(fit)), 1)
top_genes(fit, pid, n = 8)
```

```{r viz, eval = has_cebmf, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5.5}
plot_top_genes(fit, programs = head(colnames(program_scores(fit)), 2), n = 8)
```

## When to prefer which backend

- **flashier (default)**: pure R, ELBO-based null checks with a fallback
  ladder, mature on small pseudobulk problems, and the only backend with a
  `covariate_mode = "fixed"` path.
- **cebmf_torch**: torch acceleration, covariate-EBMF machinery, and loud
  failure when the fit is unusable (no silent fallback). Covariates are
  handled identically for both backends — residualized in the R
  preprocessing stage (`covariate_mode = "residualize"`, the default).

```{r session-info, echo = FALSE}
sessionInfo()
```
